grammar_concept.title: Reported Speech: backshifting tenses
grammar_concept.rule: When reporting what someone said, the tense usually moves one step back into the past (backshift): "I am tired" → She said she was tired. Pronouns and time expressions also change to fit the new context.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Quando contamos o que alguém disse (sem usar as palavras exatas, sem aspas), o tempo verbal recua um passo e os pronomes/expressões de tempo mudam para fazer sentido na nova frase.
grammar_concept.example: "I am tired," she said. → She said she was tired. "I will call you tomorrow," he said. → He said he would call me the next day.
grammar_concept.example_translation: "Estou cansada", ela disse. → Ela disse que estava cansada. "Vou ligar-te amanhã", ele disse. → Ele disse que ia ligar-me no dia seguinte.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português falado, o discurso indireto muitas vezes não muda o tempo verbal de forma rigorosa ("Ela disse que está cansada" é comum, mesmo sendo tecnicamente menos correto do que "estava"). Isto leva falantes de português a manter o tempo original em inglês também: dizem "She said she is tired" em vez de "She said she was tired" — em inglês, o recuo do tempo verbal (backshift) é praticamente obrigatório no discurso indireto.
grammar_concept.correction: Regra geral do backshift: Present Simple → Past Simple; Present Continuous → Past Continuous; Present Perfect → Past Perfect; "will" → "would"; "can" → "could". Também mudam os pronomes ("I" → "she/he") e expressões de tempo ("tomorrow" → "the next day", "today" → "that day").
grammar_concept.real_world_example: A dar um recado: "He said he would be late." (em vez de repetir "I will be late")

vocabulary.definition_en: to say that something is true, without proof
example_sentences: She claimed she had never seen him before.

vocabulary.definition_en: to agree, often reluctantly, that something is true
example_sentences: He admitted he had made a mistake.

vocabulary.definition_en: to say that something is not true

exercises.prompt: Report this: "I am tired," she said. → She said she ___ tired.
exercises.explanation: Present Simple ("am") recua para Past Simple ("was") no discurso indireto.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Manter "is" sem mudar é o erro mais comum, por transferência do português falado.

exercises.prompt: Report this: "I will call you tomorrow," he said. Choose the correct sentence.
correct_answer: He said he would call me the next day.
distractors: He said he will call me tomorrow.
He said he would call me tomorrow.
He said he would called me the next day.
exercises.explanation: "Will" recua para "would", e "tomorrow" muda para "the next day", já que o momento de referência mudou.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Manter "tomorrow" sem o mudar para "the next day" é um erro comum, mesmo entre alunos que já sabem mudar o verbo.

correct_answer: to say that something is not true
exercises.explanation: "Deny" é o oposto de "admit" — recusar que algo é verdade.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What did the manager deny?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "he denied that it was his fault."
exercises.transcript: The manager admitted the report had mistakes, but he denied that it was his fault. He claimed the data came from another department.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "In the interview, she claimed she had ten years of experience. Later, she admitted it was actually closer to five, but she denied lying on purpose." What did she admit?
correct_answer: that her experience was closer to five years
it was closer to five years
distractors: that she had ten years of experience
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "she admitted it was actually closer to five".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English (discurso indireto, frase original "I am tired"): "Ela disse que estava cansada."
exercises.explanation: "Am" recua para "was" no discurso indireto em inglês.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir sem recuar o tempo verbal ("She said she is tired") é o erro mais comum.

steps.content: "Said" is pronounced /sed/, not /seɪd/ — it doesn't rhyme with "paid" or "made", even though it looks like it should. This is one of the most commonly mispronounced words in English.

steps.prompt: Report 3 things a friend or family member recently told you, using reported speech with the correct backshift.
Write 5 sentences reporting things people said to you, using claim, admit or deny where relevant.
